questions.q: A solution containing $62g$ ethylene glycol in $250g$ water is cooled to $- {10}^{o}C$ . If ${K}_{f}$ for water is $1.86Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$ , the amount of water (in $g$ ) separated as ice is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Molecular weight of ethylene glycol

\left({C}_{2}{H}_{6}{O}_{2}\right) = 62$

Moles of ethylene glycol $= \dfrac{Wt}{M . Wt}$

$= \dfrac{62}{62} = 1$

$∆ {T}_{f} = i \times {k}_{f} \times m$

$∴ ∆ {T}_{f} = 0 - \left(- 10\right) = 10$

$i = 1$ for ethylene glycol

$∆ {T}_{f} = 1 \times 86 \times \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{250}{1000}}$

$∆ {T}_{f} = 1.86 \times 4 = 7.44$

As $∆ {T}_{f} = 10$ it implies that some amount of water has frozen and this has led to a greater depression of freezing point.

$10 = 1.86 \times \dfrac{\dfrac{62}{62}}{\dfrac{Wtof{H}_{2}O}{1000}}$

${W}_{{H}_{2}O} = 186gm$

Hence, the weight of water that has frozen~$\text{=}( 250 - 186 )gm$

$= 64gm

questions.q: The solution from the following with highest depression in freezing point/lowest freezing point is
options: $180$ g of acetic acid dissolved in $1L$of aqueous solution.
$180$ g of acetic acid dissolved in benzene
$180$ g of benzoic acid dissolved in benzene
$180$ g of glucose dissolved in water
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Depression in freezing point or elevation in melting point depends upon the number of solute particles rather than the kind of solute particles.

Depression in freezing point (${ΔT}_{f}$) is directly proportional to number of solute particles.

Also, ${ΔT}_{f}$ is directly proportional to molality.

${ΔT}_{f} = m \times {k}_{f}$

Amongst the given options acetic acid has lowest molecular mass.

The molar mass of acetic acid is $60 . 05$ g mol-1.

Hence if the molecular mass is less, molality will be more, so the lowest freezing point will be shown by $180$gm of acetic acid in $1$L aqueous solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Freezing point depression refers to the lowering of the freezing point of solvent& upon the addition of solute.& Boiling point elevation& refers to the increase in the& boiling point& of a solvent upon the addition of a solute.

$∆ {T}_{b} = {iK}_{b}m ⇒ 2 = {iK}_{b} \times 1 . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$∆ {T}_{f} = {iK}_{f}m ⇒ 2 = {iK}_{f} \times2 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

Dividing~\left(\dfrac{i}{ii}\right),$

$1 = \dfrac{Kb}{2{K}_{f}}$

${K}_{b} = 2{K}_{f}$

$

questions.q:
The osmotic pressure ($\pi$) of solutions of PVC in cyclohexanone at 300 K is measured. When a graph of $\frac{\pi}{C}$ versus concentration $C$ (in g/L) is plotted, it yields a straight line with a y-intercept of 0.0006 atm L/g. The molar mass of PVC is ______ g/mol (Nearest integer).
(Given: R = 0.083 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For a polymer solution, the relationship between osmotic pressure $\pi$ and concentration $C$ in $\text{g/L}$ is given by the virial equation:

$\dfrac{\pi}{C} = \dfrac{RT}{M} + kC$

where $M$ is the molar mass of the polymer, $R$ is the gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature.

The y-intercept of the straight line plot of $\dfrac{\pi}{C}$ versus $C$ is $\dfrac{RT}{M}$.

Equating the given y-intercept to $\dfrac{RT}{M}$:

$\dfrac{RT}{M} = 0.0006$

$M = \dfrac{RT}{0.0006}$

Substituting $R = 0.083 \text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $T = 300 \text{ K}$:

$M = \dfrac{0.083 \times 300}{0.0006}$

$M = \dfrac{24.9}{0.0006}$

$M = 41500 \text{ g/mol}$
